nodes.name: Carbon cloth activation
nodes.procedure: The commercial carbon cloth (~2 cm × 2 cm, CC) was first activated with concentrated sulfuric acid and nitric acid (3:1, v/v) at room temperature for 24 h to fully remove organic ligands on its surface before use.

nodes.name: Ni(OH)2@CC hydrothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: 4 mmol of nickel nitrate hexahydrate, 8 mmol of ammonium fluoride, and 20 mmol of urea were dissolved in 40 mL of distilled water. After that, the mixed solution was transferred into a Teflon-lined stainless-steel autoclave. The activated and dried CC sample was vertically immersed in the mixed solution and then the autoclave was sealed and heated at 110°C for 6 h. The resultant sample was washed with deionized water many times and dried at 60°C for 12 h.

nodes.name: Ni(OH)2-M@CC hydrothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: 10 mmol of nickel nitrate hexahydrate and 40 mmol of 2-methylimidazole were dissolved in 40 mL of methanol. After stirring for 20 min the mixed solution was transferred into a Teflon autoclave. Then the activated and dried CC sample was vertically immersed in the mixed solution and the autoclave was sealed and heated at 110°C for 6 h. After the reaction, the resultant sample was washed with methanol many times and dried at 60°C for 12 h.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni(OH)₂@CC shows characteristic peaks of CC substrate at 24.9° and 43.6°, with increasing intensities of β-Ni(OH)₂ (001) and (102) peaks and emergence of (006) plane at 200°C, indicating two-phase mixture of α-Ni(OH)₂ and β-Ni(OH)₂. Ni(OH)₂-M@CC shows pure phase α-Ni(OH)₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns (Figure 3a) of CC, Ni(OH)₂@CC, and Ni(OH)₂ further reveal their phase evolution processes.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni(OH)₂@CC shows uniform vertically aligned nanosheet arrays on carbon cloth surface. Ni(OH)₂-M@CC shows thin curly nanosheets 300-500 nm in length.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Typical scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images reveal that the uniform nanosheet-like Ni(OH)₂ arrays are vertically grown and orderly distributed on the carbon cloth surface (Figure 3b).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni(OH)₂ nanosheet shows lattice fringes of 2.706 Å indexed to (100) planes of β-Ni(OH)₂ with hexagonal symmetry and 120° angle indicating (002) exposed surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: A high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) image (Figure 3e) reveals the lattice fringes of 2.706Å which can be indexed to the (100) planes of β-Ni(OH)₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni(OH)₂ nanosheet in Ni(OH)₂@CC shows lattice fringes of 2.706 Å indexed to (100) planes of β-Ni(OH)₂ (JCPDS: 14-117) with hexagonal symmetry and 120° angle between crystal planes indicating exposed (002) surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: A high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) image (Figure 3e) reveals the lattice fringes of 2.706Å which can be indexed to the (100) planes of β-Ni(OH)₂ (JCPDS: 14-117). The hexagonal symmetry with a 120° angle between two crystal plane also indicates the exposed surface is the (002) plane of β-Ni(OH)₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: Elemental mapping shows uniform distribution of C, Ni, and O elements in Ni(OH)₂@CC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The elemental mapping images (Figure S8) indicate a uniform distribution of C, Ni, and O elements.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni 2p XPS shows peaks at 873.4 eV (Ni 2p₁/₂) and 855.8 eV (Ni 2p₃/₂) corresponding to Ni(OH)₂ phase. O 1s shows peaks at 528.8, 531.2, and 533.5 eV for metal-oxygen, hydroxyl, and chemisorbed water.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ni 2p XPS spectra (Figure 4b) show two major peaks of Ni2p₁/₂ and Ni2p₃/₂ with binding energies at 873.4 and 855.8 eV, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Both Ni(OH)₂@CC and Ni(OH)₂-M@CC show lattice modes at 468 and 476 cm⁻¹ for hydrogen-bonded hydroxyl groups. Ni(OH)₂@CC shows O-H stretching at 3550 cm⁻¹ from intercalated water.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Raman spectra of both Ni(OH)₂@CC and Ni(OH)₂-M@CC show the lattice modes at 468 and 476 cm⁻¹ (Figure 4d, green bar), indicating the existence of hydrogen-bonded hydroxyl groups.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni(OH)₂@CC shows O-H vibration of intercalated water, Ni-OH lattice vibration at ~700 cm⁻¹, and O-H bending at 3230-3630, 1385, 1661 cm⁻¹. Anion species detected: OCN⁻ (2187 cm⁻¹), NO₃⁻, carbonates.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The infrared spectroscopy (IR) spectroscopy (Figure 4e) also reveals the O-H vibration mode in the intercalated water molecules, the lattice vibration of Ni-OH (~700 cm⁻¹), and the O-H bending of lattice O-H or the water layer.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni(OH)₂@CC shows obvious weight loss between 100-200°C due to intercalated water removal. Ni(OH)₂-M@CC shows little crystal water.
nodes.evidence_snippet: An obvious weight loss between 100 and 200°C was observed in the Ni(OH)₂@CC sample. However, there is little crystal water detected in the Ni(OH)₂-M@CC sample.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni(OH)₂@CC and Ni(OH)₂-M@CC show good wettability. Cu shows 78.7° contact angle, CC shows superhydrophobic 157.9° contact angle.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Both Ni(OH)₂@CC and Ni(OH)₂-M@CC substrates show good wettability in both water and organic solvent, as shown in Figure 4h.
